Summary

Runway Dev gives you the official Seedance 2.5 API, available since its API launch day.

Seedance 2.5 is ByteDance’s video generation model for longer, multi-shot clips with audio, made from text, images, video or audio, and it can extend or edit clips you already have.

One generation holds several connected shots directed from the prompt, and draft mode renders a preview before the final video.

It outputs video up to 4K on text-to-video, image-to-video and video-to-video.

This page covers access, pricing, inputs and code, and how your coding agent can build the integration for you.

What is Seedance 2.5?

Seedance 2.5 is ByteDance’s video generation model for longer, multi-shot clips. It turns text, images, video and audio, alone or combined, into clips of up to 30 seconds with audio generated in the same pass, and it can extend or edit a clip you already have.

ByteDance announced it on July 31, 2026 with API access to follow, and Runway Dev offered the official model the day that API became generally available, August 7, 2026.

One generation can hold several connected shots, with the camera directed from the prompt, and draft mode makes a lower-cost preview before you pay for the final video. It renders at 480p, 720p, 1080p and 4K, with 4K available to every Runway Dev account since November 11, 2026.

Prompt

Three shots in a small café at opening time, warm morning light, handheld. One counter with an espresso machine on it and a window behind it on the left, all in the same place in every shot. Shot 1: wide from the doorway, a barista in a grey apron sets a cup under the espresso machine. Shot 2: close-up, espresso pours into the cup. Shot 3: medium across the counter, she slides the cup to a customer and says: "Careful, it's hot." Audio: the grinder, the espresso machine hissing, cups on saucers, her line spoken clearly with natural lip sync.

What are the ways to use Seedance 2.5 on Runway Dev?

Seedance 2.5 runs on Runway Dev four ways, all from one account:

Way in Best for What you need
Playground Trying a prompt, then copying the request as code A Runway Dev account
API and SDKs Calling Seedance 2.5 from your own code An API key, plus the Node or Python SDK if you want one
Coding agent Having Claude Code, Codex or Cursor build the API integration into your product, tool or pipeline The Runway Dev MCP and skills, and an API key for live calls

Seedance 2.5 is also available in Model Router, a saved config you send with the request instead of a model ID. You set what to optimize for (cost, quality or latency), a maximum cost per generation and the models allowed, and the router picks one for each request sent to POST /v1/generate/video.

How do you get API access to Seedance 2.5?

You get API access to Seedance 2.5 with a Runway Dev account and an API key:

  1. Create an account at https://dev.runway.com.
  2. Create an API key in your project’s dashboard.
  3. Add credits to your project’s balance.
  4. Store the key in your environment as RUNWAYML_API_SECRET.
  5. Send a request with "model": "seedance2_5" and the X-Runway-Version header to one of its endpoints. The code below is ready to run.

How much does the Seedance 2.5 API cost?

The Seedance 2.5 API on Runway Dev is billed per second of the video it makes, at a rate set by the output resolution: 30 credits ($0.30) per second at 720p, 68 credits ($0.68) per second at 1080p and 110 credits ($1.10) per second at 4K, and less at 480p.

Resolution Credits USD Video references
480p 20 credits per second $0.20 per second +10 credits ($0.10) per second of input
720p 30 credits per second $0.30 per second +15 credits ($0.15) per second of input
1080p 68 credits per second $0.68 per second +34 credits ($0.34) per second of input
4K 110 credits per second $1.10 per second +57 credits ($0.57) per second of input
  • Minimum 80 credits ($0.80) per generation.
  • A video reference at least 2 but under 4 seconds long is billed at 4.25 seconds, the length it is padded to.
  • Image and audio references add no charge.
  • A 5-second clip costs 100 credits ($1.00) at 480p, 150 credits ($1.50) at 720p, 340 credits ($3.40) at 1080p or 550 credits ($5.50) at 4K, before video references.

Prices current as of November 19, 2026. 1 credit = $0.01.

How the billing works:

  • Input and reference videos are billed per second, at the rate of the output’s resolution, up to the combined length the API accepts.
  • A duration of auto is billed as 30 seconds up front, and what the clip doesn’t use is refunded once it finishes.
  • Draft mode bills twice: the preview at 20 credits ($0.20) per second at 480p, and the enhanced video at 68 credits ($0.68) per second at 1080p for the same length. The preview’s charge stays as it was.
  • A task that fails input moderation (SAFETY.INPUT.*) is still charged. See task failures for what each failure means.

Prompt

Macro shot, locked-off camera: rain falls on a moss-covered stone wall, droplets bead on every strand of moss and run down the cracks in the stone, a small snail crossing slowly through the frame. Soft overcast light, sharp detail. Audio: steady rain, drips, a distant roll of thunder.

Every rate is also listed in the docs pricing guide.

What inputs does Seedance 2.5 accept?

Seedance 2.5 accepts a prompt of up to 15,000 characters, a duration of 4 to 30 seconds or auto, and images, videos and audio as inputs and references. Each endpoint uses them its own way.

On POST /v1/image_to_video you set the first and last frames, or pass images as references instead, never both in one request. A single promptImage URL is the first frame. For keyframes, send a list with a position of first, and last if you want a closing frame. For references, send a list with no position on any image: that is also the only mode that takes referenceAudio, which needs a promptText.

On POST /v1/text_to_video a request takes up to 30 images, 10 videos and 10 audio clips as references, to steer a subject, a motion or a sound. References can stand in for the prompt: a request needs a prompt or at least one reference image, video or audio clip.

On POST /v1/video_to_video, mode decides what happens to your clip. reference (the default) uses it as a reference for a new video. extend continues it with new shots that keep its characters and setting, and edit changes it in place, for example replacing the background or changing the camera’s perspective. Both need a promptText and keep the input’s aspect ratio, so they take no ratio. With edit, duration must be auto.

Here is every field, by endpoint:

POST /v1/image_to_video

Field Accepts
model (required) seedance2_5
promptImage (required) One image, or a list of images, each with an optional position of first or last (a last frame needs a first one)
promptText Text, 1 to 15,000 characters
audio true or false. Default true
seed Whole number from 0 to 4,294,967,295
outputFormat One of mp4 or mov
duration Whole number from 4 to 30, or auto
ratio One of 992:432, 854:480, 752:560, 640:640, 560:752, 480:854, 1470:630, 1280:720, 1112:834, 960:960, 834:1112, 720:1280, 2206:946, 1920:1080, 1664:1248, 1440:1440, 1248:1664, 1080:1920, 3840:1646, 3840:2160, 3840:2880, 3840:3840, 2880:3840 or 2160:3840
referenceAudio A list of up to 10 audio clips
draft true or false

POST /v1/text_to_video

Field Accepts
model (required) seedance2_5
promptText Text, 1 to 15,000 characters
audio true or false
seed Whole number from 0 to 4,294,967,295
outputFormat One of mp4 or mov
duration Whole number from 4 to 30, or auto
ratio One of 992:432, 854:480, 752:560, 640:640, 560:752, 480:854, 1470:630, 1280:720, 1112:834, 960:960, 834:1112, 720:1280, 2206:946, 1920:1080, 1664:1248, 1440:1440, 1248:1664, 1080:1920, 3840:1646, 3840:2160, 3840:2880, 3840:3840, 2880:3840 or 2160:3840
references A list of up to 30 images
referenceVideos A list of up to 10 videos
referenceAudio A list of up to 10 audio clips
draft true or false
draftTaskId A task ID

POST /v1/video_to_video

Field Accepts
model (required) seedance2_5
promptVideo (required) One video
promptText Text, 1 to 15,000 characters
audio true or false. Default true
seed Whole number from 0 to 4,294,967,295
outputFormat One of mp4 or mov
mode One of reference, extend or edit. Default reference
duration Whole number from 4 to 30, or auto
ratio One of 992:432, 854:480, 752:560, 640:640, 560:752, 480:854, 1470:630, 1280:720, 1112:834, 960:960, 834:1112, 720:1280, 2206:946, 1920:1080, 1664:1248, 1440:1440, 1248:1664, 1080:1920, 3840:1646, 3840:2160, 3840:2880, 3840:3840, 2880:3840 or 2160:3840
references A list of up to 30 images
referenceVideos A list of up to 9 videos
referenceAudio A list of up to 10 audio clips
draft true or false

Images, videos and audio go in as an HTTPS URL, a runway:// URI from an upload or a data URI; inputs lists sizes and formats. Each table shows what a field accepts on its own. Rules that combine fields are checked when the task is submitted, and the API reference has them in full.

One more rule changes what you send:

  • Draft mode makes a preview before the final video. Send draft: true and the task returns a lower-resolution preview at your aspect ratio. To enhance a preview you like, call POST /v1/text_to_video with only model and draftTaskId: any other field is rejected, and the preview has to be your own, finished and inside the enhancement window in the draft mode docs.

Inputs

  • First frame
  • Last frame

How do you use the Seedance 2.5 API?

You use the Seedance 2.5 API by sending seedance2_5 as the model to one of its endpoints. This example request, in curl, Node and Python, animates a still image with POST /v1/image_to_video, and the other fields keep their defaults:

curl

curl -X POST https://api.dev.runwayml.com/v1/image_to_video \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RUNWAYML_API_SECRET" \
  -H "X-Runway-Version: 2024-11-06" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "seedance2_5",
    "promptImage": "https://d3phaj0sisr2ct.cloudfront.net/devportal/learn/images/campaign-localizer/product-shot-b4fce78b.jpg",
    "promptText": "Locked-off camera, the glass chess knight never moves. Inside it, storm clouds drift and thin bolts of lightning flicker on and off, lighting the glass from within",
    "duration": 4
  }'

# The response carries the task id. Poll the task until it finishes:
curl https://api.dev.runwayml.com/v1/tasks/$TASK_ID \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RUNWAYML_API_SECRET" \
  -H "X-Runway-Version: 2024-11-06"

Node.js

import RunwayML, { TaskFailedError } from '@runwayml/sdk';

// Reads your API key from RUNWAYML_API_SECRET.
const client = new RunwayML();

try {
  const task = await client.imageToVideo
    .create({
      model: 'seedance2_5',
      promptImage: 'https://d3phaj0sisr2ct.cloudfront.net/devportal/learn/images/campaign-localizer/product-shot-b4fce78b.jpg',
      promptText: 'Locked-off camera, the glass chess knight never moves. Inside it, storm clouds drift and thin bolts of lightning flicker on and off, lighting the glass from within',
      duration: 4,
    })
    .waitForTaskOutput();
  console.log(task.output);
} catch (error) {
  if (error instanceof TaskFailedError) {
    console.error(error.taskDetails);
  } else {
    throw error;
  }
}

Python

from runwayml import RunwayML, TaskFailedError

# Reads your API key from RUNWAYML_API_SECRET.
client = RunwayML()

try:
    task = client.image_to_video.create(
        model="seedance2_5",
        prompt_image="https://d3phaj0sisr2ct.cloudfront.net/devportal/learn/images/campaign-localizer/product-shot-b4fce78b.jpg",
        prompt_text="Locked-off camera, the glass chess knight never moves. Inside it, storm clouds drift and thin bolts of lightning flicker on and off, lighting the glass from within",
        duration=4,
    ).wait_for_task_output()
    print(task.output)
except TaskFailedError as error:
    print(error.task_details)

Generation is asynchronous:

  • The create request returns a task ID right away, and the video is made in the background.
  • Poll GET /v1/tasks/{id} with backoff until the status is SUCCEEDED, FAILED or CANCELLED. THROTTLED means the task is waiting in a queue, not rejected.
  • Output URLs are temporary, so download the video when the task succeeds. See outputs.
  • The SDKs poll for you. waitForTaskOutput() and wait_for_task_output() raise TaskFailedError with the task’s details when it fails. They also stop waiting after a default timeout while the task keeps running, so for long clips pass a longer timeout or keep polling the task ID.
  • To use your own rules instead of one fixed model, send a Model Router’s configId to POST /v1/generate/video in place of the model. Add dryRun to see which model it picks without creating a task.

How do you generate 4K video with the Seedance 2.5 API?

You generate 4K video with Seedance 2.5 by sending a 4K pixel size as the ratio, on POST /v1/text_to_video, POST /v1/image_to_video or POST /v1/video_to_video in reference mode:

Aspect ratio 4K ratio
16:9 3840:2160
9:16 2160:3840
21:9 3840:1646
4:3 3840:2880
3:4 2880:3840
1:1 3840:3840 
curl -X POST https://api.dev.runwayml.com/v1/text_to_video \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RUNWAYML_API_SECRET" \
  -H "X-Runway-Version: 2024-11-06" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "seedance2_5",
    "promptText": "Slow aerial push over a terraced tea plantation at sunrise, mist in the valleys, workers in straw hats between the rows. Audio: birdsong and wind.",
    "ratio": "3840:2160",
    "duration": 5
  }'

In the Node and Python SDKs, set the same ratio value on the same call. What to know at 4K:

  • The rate is 110 credits ($1.10) per second at 4K, and input and reference videos add their own per-second rate, listed in the pricing table above.
  • Draft previews stay at 480p and enhanced drafts at 1080p. To get a 4K clip, send the 4K ratio on a regular request.
  • extend and edit follow the input video: they take no ratio, keep its aspect ratio and render at its resolution tier, with a 480p input rendered at 720p. A 4K input gives a 4K output, billed at the 4K rate.

Why does a Seedance 2.5 API request fail?

A Seedance 2.5 task fails with a failure code that names the cause. The common ones:

  • SAFETY.INPUT.*: content moderation rejected an input. The suffix hints at which one but may not match. The task is charged and shouldn’t be retried as is: change the inputs first.
  • SAFETY.OUTPUT.*: the generated video was rejected by moderation. Change the prompt or references before you try again.
  • ASSET.INVALID: an input file’s dimensions, duration or another property is outside what the model takes. Check it against inputs and fix it before retrying.
  • An Invalid video resolution message: an input or reference video is smaller than the minimum in inputs. Export it at a higher resolution.
  • INTERNAL.BAD_OUTPUT.01: the output failed a quality check, often because of logos, watermarks or text in the input images. Remove them and retry.
  • THIRD_PARTY.UNAVAILABLE: the model’s provider didn’t return the video, because of an outage or load. Wait, then retry.
  • A validation error on ratio or duration: values copied from another model, Seedance 2.0 included, can be outside Seedance 2.5’s lists. Take them from the inputs above.
  • An enhance request rejected: it carried fields besides model and draftTaskId, or the preview is outside the enhancement window.
  • An output link that stopped working: output URLs expire. Download the video when the task succeeds.

What does Runway Dev add when you call Seedance 2.5?

Runway Dev serves Seedance 2.5 next to Runway’s own models and other labs’ models, behind one API key and one credit balance: you build with a single key and pay a single bill, instead of an account, a key and an invoice per lab.

A coding agent can do the Seedance 2.5 integration for you on Runway Dev, end to end. Connect the Runway Dev MCP and the agent works from your live account: the models your project can call with their current prices and input limits, your credit balance and the record behind any task. It writes the integration against what the API accepts today, and when a task fails it looks up the reason and fixes it. The Runway Dev skills show the agent how to integrate with the official SDKs and how to build with models, Model Routers, Recipes and Workflows.

With Workflows, Seedance 2.5 becomes one step of a larger pipeline: chain it with Runway’s own models and other labs’ models, for images, video and audio, and run the whole pipeline with a single API call. Workflows don’t need to be built by a developer. A creative or marketing teammate builds and tests one visually in the Runway app (how Workflows work), then publishes it as an endpoint that your code calls. When the team updates the workflow, your code keeps calling the same endpoint.

FAQ

How do I get API access to Seedance 2.5?

Create a Runway Dev account at dev.runway.com, make an API key and add credits. Then send seedance2_5 as the model to any of its endpoints: POST /v1/image_to_video, POST /v1/text_to_video and POST /v1/video_to_video. To have a coding agent write the integration instead, connect the Runway Dev MCP and install the Runway Dev skills: the agent builds it from your live account, with the prices and input limits your project has today.

How much does the Seedance 2.5 API cost?

On Runway Dev, Seedance 2.5 costs 110 credits ($1.10) per second at 4K, 68 credits ($0.68) per second at 1080p, 30 credits ($0.30) per second at 720p and 20 credits ($0.20) per second at 480p, with a minimum of 80 credits ($0.80) per generation. Input and reference videos add a per-second charge, and reference images and audio add none. Prices are current as of November 19, 2026.

Is the Seedance 2.5 API on Runway Dev the official model?

Runway Dev’s Seedance 2.5 API runs the official Seedance 2.5 model from ByteDance, offered since the day its API became generally available. You call it with your Runway Dev API key and the model ID seedance2_5, like every other model on Runway Dev.

Can I use Seedance 2.5 without writing code?

You can use Seedance 2.5 on Runway Dev without writing code yourself. The playground sends a request from a form and gives it back as code, and a coding agent connected to the Runway Dev MCP writes the integration for you. A creative or marketing teammate can also build a workflow around Seedance 2.5 in the Runway app and publish it as an endpoint your app calls.

Does the same Runway Dev API key work for Seedance 2.5 and other models?

One Runway Dev API key calls Seedance 2.5 and every other model your project can use, Runway’s own and other labs’, with the same SDKs, task flow and credit balance. Switching models means changing the model field, or the rules of a Model Router.

What is the Seedance 2.5 model ID on Runway Dev?

The model ID is seedance2_5, and it is the same on all of its endpoints: POST /v1/image_to_video, POST /v1/text_to_video and POST /v1/video_to_video.

How long can a Seedance 2.5 video be, and at what resolutions?

A Seedance 2.5 clip on Runway Dev runs 4 to 30 seconds, or set duration to auto and the model picks the length. It comes out at 480p, 720p, 1080p and 4K, chosen through the ratio you send, with 3840:2160 for 16:9 4K and 2160:3840 for vertical 4K.

How many references can Seedance 2.5 use through the API?

Seedance 2.5 takes up to 30 images, 10 videos and 10 audio clips as references on POST /v1/text_to_video. On POST /v1/video_to_video it takes up to 30 images, 9 videos and 10 audio clips, alongside the clip you send. On POST /v1/image_to_video, up to 30 reference images go in promptImage as a list with no position (a single URL is read as the first frame), and the request can add up to 10 audio clips.

What is Seedance 2.5 draft mode, and how is it billed?

Draft mode makes a Seedance 2.5 preview first and the final video only when you ask for it. Send draft: true, then enhance the preview with a POST /v1/text_to_video request that carries only model and draftTaskId. The preview is billed at 20 credits ($0.20) per second at 480p and the enhanced video at 68 credits ($0.68) per second at 1080p, as two separate charges.

Can Seedance 2.5 edit or extend an existing video through the API?

Seedance 2.5 extends and edits clips on POST /v1/video_to_video. Set mode to extend to continue a clip or edit to change it in place, and describe the change in promptText.

Why did my Seedance 2.5 request fail with SAFETY.INPUT.TEXT?

SAFETY.INPUT.TEXT means content moderation rejected an input of your request; the suffix hints at the prompt but may not match. The task is charged and shouldn’t be retried as is, so change the prompt or inputs before you send it again.

Can I switch from Seedance 2.5 to another video model without changing my code?

A Model Router lets you change models without touching your code. Send its configId to POST /v1/generate/video, and change the models it may use, its priority or its cost cap in the router.

Runway’s Seedance 2.5 prompt guide covers how to structure a Seedance 2.5 prompt.
